Goal tracking frames

Source: R/tracking.R
nhl_goal_tracking.Rd

The NHL replays every goal from puck and player tracking: about 14 seconds of every skater, both goalies and the puck, ten frames a second, for every goal from 2023-24 on. nhl_goal_tracking() returns those frames, one row per object per frame, with positions in feet from centre ice in the play-by-play's orientation (x along the rink, y across it).

Usage

nhl_goal_tracking(game_id, event_id)

nhl_goal_replay(game_id, event_id)

Arguments

game_id

Ten-digit NHL game id.

event_id

The goal's event id in the play-by-play (event_id in nhl_pbp()).

Value

nhl_goal_tracking(): a tibble with columns frame, time (seconds from the first frame), entity_id, is_puck, player_id, sweater_number, team, x, y. The goal's game and event ids ride along as attributes. nhl_goal_replay(): a one-row tibble.

Details

The files live on wsr.nhle.com and answer only requests that come from nhl.com, so the request says it does (a Referer header). nhl_goal_replay() is the goal itself as the NHL's replay page has it: scorer, assists, strength, the score, both clubs' logos and the highlight video.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
frames <- nhl_goal_tracking(2025020534, 777)
plot_goal(frames)
nhl_goal_replay(2025020534, 777)
}
